sources.entry: DAViCal - Server for calendar sharing (CalDAV) that uses a PostgreSQL database as a data store. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 PHP/deb

summary.name: DAViCal
summary.one_liner: DAViCal is a free, GPL-licensed CalDAV calendar sharing server that stores calendar data in an SQL (PostgreSQL) database.
use_cases: Syncing calendars with CalDAV clients like Evolution, Mozilla Lightning, or iOS
Delegating read/write calendar access to other users
Scheduling meetings with free/busy time display
Hosting a self-hosted CalDAV server on Debian or Linux
summary.what_it_does: DAViCal implements the CalDAV protocol for storing iCalendar-format calendar resources on a remote shared server. It uses an SQL database, specifically PostgreSQL, to store event data. It supports delegation of read/write access between calendar users and lets multiple users or clients read and write the same calendar entries. It also supports scheduling meetings with free/busy time displayed, and offers WebDAV access in read-only or read-write mode (read-write noted as not recommended). The project says it aims to interoperate with as many CalDAV clients as possible.
notable: Uses PostgreSQL as its data store
Free software under the GNU General Public License (GPL-2.0)
caveats: Requires a PostgreSQL database server and a PHP 5 capable web server
Windows is not recommended by the project
WebDAV read-write mode is noted as not recommended
